precepts.text: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, save thyself, and come down from the cross. This is Christ on the cross.
precepts.point: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?
precepts.why:
This is Christ on the cross. “And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days, Save thyself, and come down from the cross.”

They mocked him with the very words of John 2:19, still thinking he had boasted about the building in Jerusalem. But there he was, hanging on the cross: the temple he spoke of was being destroyed right in front of them, and they could not see it.

So we know Christ was talking about his body. “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: they destroyed his body on the cross, and in three days he raised it up again. What the passersby railed at as a failed boast was the prophecy being fulfilled before their eyes.

precepts.text: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.
precepts.point: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him. It was written all over their face, all over their spirit. They could not hide it. Even a heathen would see that. And do we see that today? Yes. You have heathens making videos where they'll sit down with other heathens and say, okay, this camp believes in this, this camp believes in that. This camp is worldwide; they are an organized movement, they're global, they're not domestic. And this camp right here with the studs on, looking like the Legion of Doom from WWF, these guys over here hate these men in purple. Even the heathens know it. That is a damn shame.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

precepts.why:
Matthew says Pilate “knew that for envy they had delivered him”, and Mark says it plainly: “For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.” Pilate was a heathen, and even he could see it. It was written all over their face, all over their spirit. They could not hide it.

Do we see that today? Yes. You have heathens making videos where they sit down with other heathens and say, this camp believes in this, this camp believes in that. This camp is worldwide; they are an organized movement, global, not domestic. And this camp right here with the studs on, looking like the Legion of Doom from WWF, these guys over here hate these men in purple.

Even the heathens know it. That is a damn shame. The envy that delivered Christ is the same envy the heathen can see today.
